- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a sharp drop, allow a 1–2 day lag in forecast adjustment to avoid premature rebound.  
- After a forecast spike (e.g., >+2% from recent mean), cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at +1.5% above peak to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 2–3 days, shift forecast horizon slightly backward (e.g., 1–2 days earlier) for 30d horizon.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, apply mean reversion: if forecast is >+1.5% above 14d moving average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.  
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.4% per day to avoid overestimating continuation.
